## 7. Hostile validation (HV) and review

Review and hostile-validation (HV) guidance (operator-directed, 2026-10-09). Applies to every agent, plan, and review loop.

### 7.1 Adversarial review of tracked results (locked 2026-08-12)

1. Validate independently through a hostile reviewer wherever the plan calls for HV and before any done state (section 4.5). Self-check alone is not validation.
2. Every result is timestamped with a sortable local date and time (section 3.1).
3. Every FAIL and UNKNOWN from the review is shown to the operator.
4. Every result includes an accuracy rating and a completeness rating.

Reviewer (resolution of 2026-10-13, verbatim): "HV must not be executed by the same agent family as the requesting agent.  If not specified by operator, ask what agent and model to use for HV in a session." HV uses the reviewer and tooling explicitly authorized for the session. Verify the reviewer's model and effort from its own runtime receipts.

Review time is unbounded (operator, 2026-10-12, verbatim: "Do not bound review time"): no timeout, kill, deadline, or wait limit on any HV reviewer run, and no expected duration in briefs or plans; the implementer only checks the response stream in repeated read-only waits until the run completes, however long the review takes.

HV is not bounded by size either, and a stall is the one reason to end a reviewer (added 2026-10-28; operator, 2026-10-28T21:57:09, verbatim: "HV invocations should not be bounded by time or size.  Only if it stops updating for longet than 30 minutes should you kill it."): no cap on the evidence a request supplies or on what the reviewer reads or writes (briefs carry no file-size limit); end the reviewer only when its response stream has had no update for more than 30 minutes, record that run as stopped, not evidence, and relaunch. Committing a receipt GitHub refuses as a compressed copy, with the original kept, is not a bound on the review.

When HV runs (resolution of 2026-10-13, verbatim): "HV cadence is an artifact of the plan, not a standing rule." Section 4.5 still requires hostile AGREE before any done state.

HV at a phase exit (approved 2026-11-03): when the plan calls for HV at a phase's exit, HV runs only when that phase's work is complete with no code pending and its full gate set is green at the final head (operator, 2026-10-21: "If it needs code, it's not ready for HV."). A run that stops without a verdict is not a DISAGREE. While its HV is paused, the phase starts no new work.

Test evidence is supplied by the request; the reviewer never builds or runs tests (added 2026-10-27): section 7.9.

### 7.2 Mandatory scope (locked 2026-08-13; operations versus requirements locked 2026-08-14)

Operator directive (verbatim intent): hostile validation must test for workspace rule violations, requirement violations, and the current plan holistically, in addition to the requested validation. Mandatory attack surfaces on every run:
1. Requested validation: every implementer claim (pass, done, green, fixed, SHAs, test counts, receipts).
2. Workspace rules: honesty, receipts, MCP-only TODO, session, and requirement storage when the workspace uses the MCP server, PowerShell only, no Python. BDPv4 and related directives pertain only to code and documentation in the scope of implementing the project. Phase order (requirements drive tests; tests before implementation) is caught by a hostile review between phases of plan implementation. Do not fail it solely by comparing FR `createdAt` to test or implementation file times after the slice is written. Do not apply BDPv4 to user-directed operations.
3. Requirements: apply to project requirement work only (product features, implementation, claimed-complete plan steps). FR, TR, TEST, AC, and mappings are required there; missing FR, TR, or AC for claimed-complete implementation work is FAIL.
4. Current plan holistically: when the implementer claims plan-step completion, check the plan's definition of done, blockers, amendments, and exit criteria. A user-directed operational action does not have to satisfy an unrelated plan's definition of done unless it claimed that plan step done.

Two work classes:
1. Project implementation scope: product code, product tests, project documentation, and plan-step completion for that implementation. BDPv4 and related directives pertain only to this class. Missing FR, TR, TEST, or AC for claimed-complete implementation work is FAIL on surface 3.
2. User-directed general actions: operator-ordered lab or operations work that is not a product requirement (for example: uninstall an obsolete package, back up a device, pair wireless ADB, take a screenshot, copy a store the operator named, remove a leftover launcher). These are not FR, TR, or TEST. Surface 3 must not FAIL for "no FR or TR for this uninstall" or equivalent.

How the reviewer classifies: classify the request first and record the class on the receipt. If the operator explicitly directed the action, default to class 2 unless the implementer also shipped product code or claimed a plan or FR complete. Do not invent a requirements gap to punish class-2 work. If class-2 work is mixed with class-1 product changes in the same turn, score them separately and FAIL surface 3 only on the class-1 slice. What still applies to class-2 work: surface 1 (did they do the directed action, with receipts), surface 2 (honesty, receipts, look before delete, PowerShell, no Python, MCP-only storage; not BDPv4 for the operation itself), and surface 4 only if they claim an active plan step is complete.

OverallVerdict is AGREE only if all applicable surfaces PASS; surface 3 is not applicable (not a FAIL) for class-2 operator actions. A parent agent must not under-scope the brief to code-only claims on class-1 work; if it does, the reviewer expands and still evaluates the applicable surfaces. A code-only brief that omits BDPv4, requirements, or the plan is non-compliant.

The reviewer executes the add-profile skill before beginning its validation work, every run including resume, and its receipt records that it ran.

### 7.3 Score gate and the bar (locked 2026-09-10)

A hostile validation passes only when both its accuracy score and completeness score are at least 98 percent. Any individual score below 98 is a failure; OverallVerdict must be DISAGREE when either score is below 98, even if the FAIL and UNKNOWN counts are both zero. If a reviewer emits a verdict without numeric accuracy and completeness scores, the HV is incomplete: treat it as DISAGREE until scores are present and at least 98. The threshold is an acceptance threshold, not a target reviewers may game or inflate. A sub-98 score cannot authorize any goal, TODO, requirement, or plan done-state change: display it as a failure, remediate, and rerun.

98/98 HV (accuracy and completeness) is the bar for a functioning system, not perfection. Never lower, skip, or approve below it; lower thresholds let real bugs through that later become blocking test failures. When rounds stop converging, fix the process, never the threshold. "98/98 is not perfection, it is functional." Never propose lowering it (added 2026-10-13, from the operator's ruling of 2026-10-09).

### 7.4 Receipts and the session log (locked 2026-09-10)

Operator directive (verbatim intent): HV requests must have request and response logged as jsonl files; the results of HV validation must be saved in their entirety to the MCP session log.

1. Request jsonl: one JSON object per line covering the HV ask as sent: sortable local timestamp, workspace path, reviewer identity (agent, model, effort), launch command, prompt or body, named evidence paths, and the gate or TODO under review.
2. Response jsonl: the reviewer's full machine stream as jsonl (for a CLI reviewer, its full event stream, every start, tool, message, and completion line; for a subagent reviewer, one object per reviewer message or tool result, then a final object with the complete verdict).
3. Durable locations, in order: the workspace `docs/receipts/hv/{timestamp}-{gate}.request.jsonl` and `.response.jsonl` ({timestamp} is the sortable local date and time in file-safe form, yyyyMMddTHHmmss); otherwise a durable user-level receipts directory named for the workspace. Never only a temp or scratch tree that can be wiped.
4. Build jsonl from native objects and serialize. PowerShell only; no Python; no handwritten JSON.
5. The reviewer's session-log turn stores the entire result: the complete verdict prose, every finding, every PASS, FAIL, or UNKNOWN item, the scores, OverallVerdict, thread, session, and request ids, the complete VERDICT JSON object, absolute paths to the request and response jsonl, and proof the turn persisted (a history query or equivalent). If a field is too large for one write, split it across ordered dialog or action items on the same turn; never omit findings to fit. The jsonl files remain the byte-complete stream; the session log still carries the full verdict text, not a digest.
6. Every reviewer creates complete session-log turns for every review: bootstrap if needed, open a dedicated review session or a clear review turn, begin the turn, append dialog and actions with integer order values, complete or fail the turn, and prove persistence in the receipt. A review without a complete session-log turn is incomplete, even if its claim verdicts would pass.
7. Progress entries (MEMORY-PREFERENCE-003, verbatim; added 2026-10-13 from PAYTON-LEGION2): "For every future hostile validation (HV) session, require the reviewer to emit progress entries into its durable response JSONL during the run at meaningful intervals, not backfill or consolidate them at the end. Each progress entry must include a numeric completion percentage and an estimated time remaining (ETA). Include this requirement in every HV launch prompt and preserve the entries in the durable response JSONL." The reviewer's ETA is its own report; it never becomes a timeout or a bound on review time (section 7.1).

Forbidden: HV with no request jsonl or no response jsonl; HV whose only record is temp or scratch; AGREE without accuracy and completeness both at or above 98; summarizing HV into the session log instead of storing the entire result; marking a goal, TODO, or plan done on incomplete HV.

### 7.5 Before every HV round

- Read the whole plan and every document under review end to end; targeted checks are not holistic. When the operator asks for a reconciliation or projection of problems before HV, present every projected problem to the operator and get confirmation before launching the review (added 2026-10-13, from the operator's rulings of 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-13).
- Run a structured what-if pass per requirement, not only a consistency check. Ask what observably happens under: crash, restart, or replay at each step; ordering and concurrency; boundary and malformed input; each host or plugin, including unsupported ones; lifecycle (clear, resume, end, terminal states); isolation (cross-workspace, cross-session, cross-agent); legacy and upgrade; operator-visible output. Where the plan does not state the outcome, add a valid AC tagged with the plan's phase or slice and a named test. Adding a valid AC is always a win.
- Chain rules together to find deadlocks: rules that each pass alone but together leave no accepted remedy.
- Diff against known-good anchors and ask "How did it deviate? How do we get back in line?": (1) the operator's verbatim decisions, (2) current working code and baseline-green behavior, (3) classic patterns such as idempotency keys, transactional outbox with at-least-once delivery and idempotent consumers (never claim exactly-once), write-ahead journal before mutation, optimistic concurrency. Justify any departure explicitly or return to the pattern.
- Check that every field set and code list is defined once and identically everywhere, every mapping edge is backed by a TEST statement and vice versa, and handoff and TODO metadata match the plan.
- Edit only between rounds, never while a round is running.
- Propagation audit: after changing any rule, field set, code, or outcome, search every place that states it (requirements, ACs, TRs, TESTs, wire contracts, use cases, the plan's phase or slice tasks, host tables, handoff, TODO) and update each one, or replace the copies with a reference to one canonical statement. In one review round, three of six findings were rules changed in one place and left stale elsewhere. Large edit batches need this audit most.
- Prefer a traceable key over content matching when pairing records (for example queue position or a shared id rather than a text hash); content can differ in representation between producers.
- Search before adding, and lint mechanically: before writing any new rule, grep the whole document for an existing rule on the same subject; a second rule is a contradiction even if each is fine alone (one round added a two-AC TEST rule beside an existing three-AC one). Check cross-reference classes (FR->TR->TEST mappings, which of the plan's phases or slices owns each named case, phase order) with a small script instead of waiting for the reviewer to find them one per round.
- Enforce the checklist, do not just remember it (operator, 2026-10-10, after this guidance was skipped for many unsupervised rounds): make the pre-HV checklist a hard gate in the HV launcher, which refuses a round unless a per-round self-review record shows evidence for each item (holistic review, what-if, propagation audit, phase boundaries, search-before-adding, no new mechanism, mapping lint, the operator scoping directive verbatim in the brief, standing rules in every delegated brief). Guidance that only lives in memory gets skipped under time pressure.
- Phase-boundary audit: every test or AC you add must be allocated to the plan's phase or slice where everything it depends on already exists (server gate, review verbs, marker fields). A behaviour that ships before its dependency needs an explicit activation contract (for example a server-written capability) and an inert mode, including after a rollback. Check the dependency chain and the rollout order for each new case, not just the AC text.

### 7.6 When findings come back

- Ask "What did I miss?", not only "How do I fix this?". Classify each finding (crash window, cross-session addressing, traceability drift, field-set drift, use case vs requirement contradiction, metadata drift, and so on) and sweep the whole artifact for siblings of each class before the next round.
- Verify each finding against source before acting.
- Separate implementer fixes from operator decisions, and batch operator decisions into one question.
- Recurrence signal: when one design area produces new findings in round after round, the problem is structural, usually a missing traceable key or a missing single source of truth. Stop patching. Diff the area against the known-good pattern (for example single writer, one ordered log, idempotency key), return to it, and delete the mechanism the patches added. One design area failed for five rounds until a single minter reading one ordered log replaced the patches.
- Indistinguishable inputs: when two histories produce byte-identical inputs (a redelivery of one event versus a separate event with equal fields), no derived key can separate them. Adding per-invocation state such as a counter or salt breaks idempotence instead. Run the what-if on both histories, then state the honest limit: fail closed under an existing rule, probe how often it happens, and document it. Never promise two invariants the inputs cannot support. Before a fix, check it against every invariant the old value satisfied (purity, retry reuse, the two-process tests), not only the finding it repairs.

### 7.7 Writing fixes

- Fix the deficient requirement. Reconcile with existing requirements first, strengthen an existing AC second, create a new requirement only when the need is genuinely new.
- Do not add design mechanism (protocols, algorithms, crash choreography) to plan text. State the observable, testable outcome; the how belongs to the contract step of the plan's phase or slice.
- Make each fix minimal, then attack it yourself before the next round; fixes are the main source of new findings. Do not churn text that a prior round accepted.

### 7.8 Design principle and coordination

- Always have a traceable relationship when coordinating two disparate entities: every record, event, or message carries the root ids of whatever it is a child of or depends on, so it is attributable on its own. A missing parent id is a design failure. Find the commonality first when relating something new to existing knowledge. Where an external format lacks the key, say so and compensate in your own records; never infer it silently.
- Coordinating with another agent: use one append-only channel with read-back verification. (The global memory MEMORY-PROCESS-007 was that channel until the operator had it removed on 2026-11-06; its last text is archived, unread, under `/home/sharpninja/.claude/profile-archive/20261106T1140-global-memory-removals/`.) Accept counters that expose real defects; fold refinements in only as minimal ACs. Each effort keeps its own required reviewer and gates; keep cross-effort dependencies acyclic and order-independent. A decision relayed by one agent may not satisfy the other agent's approval controls; the operator may need to state it to each agent directly.

### 7.9 The request supplies the test evidence; the reviewer never builds or runs tests (added 2026-10-27)

Operator, 2026-10-27T04:35, typos fixed at the operator's request (04:40, "That is correct.  Please fix any typos", confirming that the abbreviation meant the HV reviewer and the scope of the current review): "HV requests must supply TRX files for all unit tests in the repo, and for any integration tests specific to the scope of the HV review. The HV reviewer is not to build code or run tests independently. If the HV reviewer feels the tests are inadequate, then it should fail the review and propose additional AC and tests."

How to apply:
- The HV request supplies the TRX files themselves, not summaries: every unit test project in the repository, and every integration test run within the review's scope (for example each host's integration lane and each hostile-environment run the plan requires), from the gate runs at the head under review. The request JSONL and the brief name each file's path with its run id, host, head and command. A request that lacks one of them is incomplete and is not launched.
- The reviewer does not build code, restore packages, or run tests, test projects or build targets, independently or in a sandbox. It judges from the supplied TRX files, the sources, git history, the receipts and the live stores read only. Reading files and running read-only inspection queries or scripts over the evidence is not building or testing.
- If the reviewer judges the tests inadequate (missing, weak, environment- or platform-dependent, or not covering an acceptance criterion), it FAILs the review and proposes the additional acceptance criteria and tests, each named and stated, as findings. It never substitutes its own test runs for missing evidence.
- Every brief and launcher carries this rule; a brief that invites the reviewer to rerun builds, targets or tests is non-compliant.

These rules apply in every workspace that uses the operator's MCP server and its agent plugin.

- The workspace's own `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` are the authority for the plugin contract, its endpoints, and its startup validation. Operative rule that must never be dropped: "Not in the visible tool list" does not mean unavailable; use the documented wrapper invocation form.

### 8.1 Who logs what

- Agents always log (added 2026-10-13; operator, verbatim: "BG agents should NEVER skip logging.  NEVER."): every agent that does work (a subagent, a background agent, a reviewer) opens, updates, and completes its own session-log turn through the plugin route and reports its session and request ids; no brief may tell an agent to stay out of the session log.
- One turn per real request, per agent (resolution of 2026-10-13: "Per request, per agent"): each agent logs one turn for each real request it handles; a subagent's turn carries the parent turn's session and request ids (section 7.8), so the work is attributable without counting the request twice. Replace real turns canceled by a later open.
- A background event with no work of its own (a completion notice) is not an agent: its hook-opened turn is failed as system_event_phantom, and the work it reports is logged by the agent that does it (resolution of 2026-10-13: "Events aren't agents").

### 8.2 Decisions are conclusions

In the session log, decisions are conclusions and judgments with their consequences, not the steps taken. They go in the turn's design decisions, distinct from its actions. Every sync or wrap-up pass enumerates the real judgment calls of the turn and logs them. Never report "0 decisions (folded into actions)"; that phrasing is the failure mode itself.

Why: the operator has been trying to get agents to log session decisions reliably since February 2026. The pattern: the keystroke trail (actions) gets captured while the reasoning (design decisions) is under-recorded or buried inside action text. He pays for the reasoning, not just the steps. On 2026-06-29 the first sync pass of a 12-round review loop logged 0 decisions and called them "folded into actions", exactly the gap he has been fighting. He flagged it directly: "Decisions are about your conclusions, not the actions you take" and "It feels like you have been deliberately avoiding session logging... especially details of decisions."

How to apply: on every sync or wrap-up, after appending actions, explicitly list the conclusions made this turn, each as judgment plus consequence plus affected requirements or files, and write them to design decisions, append-only (read existing first, send existing plus new, preserve order). A turn that made genuine judgment calls but logs zero decisions is a red flag; re-check before reporting. Heavy reads can time out and render existing decisions blank; that is a read artifact, not an empty section, so re-read before assuming you must recreate. Write the decision when it happens; do not reconstruct it later.

### 8.3 Turn titles summarize the request

Session-log turn titles are a concise summary of the operator's request: never the literal placeholder "User prompt", and not a verbatim first-line truncation of the prompt.

Why: the operator reviews the session log by turn title; "User prompt" and raw first lines make turns unscannable and indistinguishable.

How to apply: when opening, updating, or completing a turn, set the title to a short request summary. The plugin's prompt hook auto-titles from the prompt's first line and falls back to "User prompt" on empty prompts (Stop-hook continuation turns hit this); the hook cannot summarize, so the agent must refine the title. Never leave a turn titled "User prompt".

213	
214	  - Never edit YAML files by appending, replacing, or removing text lines. This includes one-key configuration changes.

220	  ## MCP and Plugin Failure Reporting
221	  - MCP Server failures and required-plugin failures discovered while working must always be written as a normal failsafe YAML report. Use the plugin/REPL failsafe or pending YAML queue and preserve the triage method (`workflow.triage.report`, `triage_report`, or equivalent plugin triage tool) plus title, summary, observed behavior, expected behavior, severity, component, workspace path, dedupe key or error signature, affected paths, evidence, reproduction hints, tags, reporter agent, session id, turn id, and current TODO id when known.

223	  - Do not create TODOs, requirements, GitHub issues, manual repair plans, or alternate reports for MCP Server/plugin failures unless the user's active request is to fix that failure.

227	  ## Agent Help (MCP Server issues)
228	  When you are stuck on any MCP Server surface (marker trust, plugin bootstrap, session log, TODO, requirements, triage, memory, context search, federation, hooks, or API behavior), request expert help instead of improvising raw REST bypasses.

REST: `POST /mcpserver/agent-help/session` then WebSocket `/mcpserver/agent-help/session/{id}/stream` (SSE fallback: `POST .../turn/stream`).
231	  - **Caller obligations:** include reproduction steps, exact error text, and files already consulted. Do not instruct the helper to ignore guardrails, skip triage, or mutate TODO/session-log/requirements storage directly.

234	  ## MCP Memories
235	  MCP memories are durable operator guidance managed by the MCP Server. Global memories apply to every workspace; Workspace memories apply only to the active workspace. Memory IDs use `MEMORY-{CATEGORY}-{NNN}`.
236	  Agents that support request-boundary injection must render required memories exactly as:
237	  REQUIRED MEMORIES - MEMORY-REQ-001: Raw memory text.
238	  If no required memories are visible, render:
239	  REQUIRED MEMORIES - None.
240	  Preserve raw memory text exactly; do not summarize, paraphrase, reorder within a scope, silently generate new memories, or add secrets. MCP memories are not a secret store. Effective memory order is Global memories first sorted by ID, then current Workspace memories sorted by ID.
241	  Existing agent-local memory stores are caches or migration sources only; the MCP memory store is the authoritative shared record. Import agent-local memories only when the operator approves the scope, the content belongs to this workspace or is intentionally Global, and the import does not leak secrets, private notes, or unrelated workspace guidance.
242	  Attribute memory mutations with the real agent or user identity via `updatedBy` when supported, and record successful memory add/update/remove operations in the active session log through `workflow.sessionlog.appendActions`. Keep import provenance in the session log or dialog instead of adding private source paths to memory text.
243	  Manage memories through the required plugin or MCP tool surface: `memory_add`, `memory_list`, `memory_update`, `memory_remove`, `memory_remember`, `memory_recall`, `memory_explore`, `memory_consolidate`, `memory_promote`, `memory_revert`; REPL `workflow.memory.add`, `workflow.memory.list`, `workflow.memory.update`, `workflow.memory.remove`, `workflow.memory.remember`, `workflow.memory.recall`, `workflow.memory.explore`, `workflow.memory.consolidate`, `workflow.memory.promote`, `workflow.memory.revert`; or REST `/mcpserver/memory` when explicitly allowed for non-plugin diagnostics.

252	  ## PowerShell.MCP Command Routing
253	  For every PowerShell Core (`pwsh`) invocation on every operating system:
254	  - Use PowerShell.MCP 1.14.0 or newer from PSGallery as the command runner. Install or update it with `Install-PSResource PowerShell.MCP` when the agent environment does not provide a current version.
255	  - `execute_command` is the primary MCP tool for PowerShell cmdlets, CLI tools, navigation, builds, tests, file-system work, and process management. Do not use the removed `invoke_expression` name. Host-qualified names depend on the configured server key: for example, `mcp__powershell__execute_command` for `powershell` and `mcp__pwsh__execute_command` for `pwsh`.
256	  - Calling `start_console` first is optional because `execute_command` auto-starts or reuses a console. Call `start_console` explicitly only to pre-warm at `start_location`, show a banner, allocate a sub-agent console, or force an additional console by supplying `reason`; omit `reason` when reuse is preferred.
257	  - Use `get_current_location` when the current PowerShell context matters. For a sub-agent, call `start_console` with `is_subagent=true`, retain the returned `agent_id`, and pass it on every later PowerShell.MCP tool call.
258	  - When a command continues after the call returns, use `wait_for_completion` to retrieve the cached result instead of running `Start-Sleep`. Use `cancel` for an interruptible pipeline or native CLI, and `close_console` for a non-interruptible command or PowerShell host prompt. If `close_console` reports that a human is typing, only repeat the same PID call when confirming that the console should be closed.
259	  - In 1.14.0, blocking timeouts are end-to-end deadlines and are capped at 170 seconds for Claude Code and 50 seconds for other or unidentified clients unless a lower limit applies. A timed-out command keeps running and its result is cached for a later tool call.
260	  - Route `pwsh` commands through a PowerShell.MCP session instead of launching ad hoc PowerShell processes. On Windows, reuse one session for the workspace and route `node` invocations through it as well.
261	  - When PowerShell.MCP must launch PowerShell Core directly, invoke `pwsh.exe` with `-NoProfile -NonInteractive`. Do not use `powershell.exe`.
262	  - The PowerShell escape character is the backtick `` ` ``, not the backslash. Never use C or bash-style `\"` escaping inside PowerShell command strings.
263	  - Prefer single-quoted PowerShell strings for literal regex, paths, JSON/YAML snippets, and text containing pipeline characters such as `|`.
264	  - When a command needs nested quoting, choose one of these patterns before improvising: `-File` with explicit arguments; piping stdin to the called tool or script; single-quoted or double-quoted here-strings; `-EncodedCommand` for complex inline PowerShell; or correct backtick escaping for embedded PowerShell quotes.
265	  - If a regex or literal argument contains `|`, `&`, `;`, parentheses, braces, or quotes, verify it is inside a single PowerShell argument before running.
266	  - For text reads and edits inside PowerShell.MCP, use `Show-TextFiles`, `Add-LinesToFile`, `Update-LinesInFile`, `Update-MatchInFile`, and `Remove-LinesFromFile`; pass literal content through `var1` to `var4`. Version 1.12.0 and newer stage replacements beside the target, so do not apply the obsolete same-volume `TEMP`/`TMP` workaround. Re-read or diff every edit before claiming it landed.

283	  1. Treat the first 401 (or a /health failure) as a restart signal and stop using the cached API key immediately.
284	  2. Re-read this marker file (AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml) for the rotated apiKey and current endpoints.
285	  3. Re-verify trust before resuming: recompute the marker signature with the new key and call /health with a fresh nonce.
286	  4. Re-bootstrap and resume through your required agent plugin. Codex: run `Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin.ps1 -Command Status` to re-establish marker trust, health nonce, workspace, and the current session/turn, then continue with `Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin.ps1 -Command Invoke -Method <method> -Params <yaml>`. Other agents: re-run the plugin session-start hook/command, then continue via the plugin session tools.
287	  5. Recover the open turn instead of starting over: query session history through the plugin (workflow.sessionlog.queryHistory), find the in-progress turn, then keep updating and complete it via the plugin. Do not open a duplicate session for the same work.
288	  5a. Treat `deprecated: true` on successful `workflow.*` results as metadata, not wrapper failure. Treat an empty `workflow.sessionlog.queryHistory` result as a valid no-match result. Re-check the workspace current directory, explicit `agent` or `sourceType`, and plugin cache/session state through the wrapper; do not use raw REST merely because history is empty or marked deprecated.

prompt: |
  You are connected to an MCP Context Server at http://LAB-OMARCHY:7147. Use this server to coordinate your work.

  ## Session Start (Run Once Per Session)
  1. Read this marker file for connection details and API key.
  2. Bootstrap the required plugin named for your agent in the top-level `agent_plugins` contract. Get the plugin through the MCP Server tool registry before relying on local root hints: search `/mcpserver/tools/search?keyword=<plugin_name>` for the installed tool definition and select the result whose `name` exactly equals `<plugin_name>`; if that exact tool definition is missing, install the definition from `/mcpserver/tools/buckets/official/install?toolName=<plugin_name>`, then search again. Execute the exact tool definition's returned `commandTemplate` with `targetParent` set to the plugin parent directory to clone or update the plugin repository. Codex must use `mcpserver-codex-plugin`; Claude must use `mcpserver-claude-code-plugin`; Copilot must use `mcpserver-copilot-plugin`; Cline must use `mcpserver-cline-plugin`; Grok must use `mcpserver-grok-plugin`.
  3. Verify the marker signature using the workspace API key in this file before contacting the server.
  4. Call /health with a random nonce and confirm the response echoes that exact nonce.
  5. Verify and log plugin identity before other MCP work: sourceType, plugin name/version, plugin root or MCP server name, marker signature result, health nonce result, and workspace path.
  6. Review recent session history and current TODOs only after signature, nonce, and plugin verification succeed.
  7. Post an initial session log turn for the session.

  ## Required Agent Plugins
  - `agent_plugins.policy` is `required`. The plugin contract or deterministic digest is covered by marker signature verification. - Plugin acquisition is the bootstrap exception to the normal plugin-only rule: if the matching plugin is not already available locally, use the authenticated tool registry endpoints in this marker to locate/install the matching `mcpserver-*-plugin` tool definition from the `official` bucket and run its clone/update command. After acquisition, bootstrap and use the matching plugin for normal MCP work. - If your matching plugin cannot be acquired through the tool registry or remains unavailable after acquisition, stop MCP usage, record `MCP_PLUGIN_UNAVAILABLE:<Agent>`, and continue only with non-MCP local diagnosis. - Do not substitute raw REST, generic `mcpserver-repl`, helper modules, or another agent's plugin for normal session, TODO, requirements, import/export, or traceability operations. - Another agent's plugin may be inspected only for read-only diagnosis of plugin installation or contract drift. - Normal workspace shell commands use `pwsh.exe`. Plugin-owned hooks may use the runner declared by that plugin contract. - Codex plugin tools/hooks must satisfy `agent_plugins.agents.Codex`; Claude plugin tools/hooks must satisfy `agent_plugins.agents.Claude`; Copilot plugin tools/hooks must satisfy `agent_plugins.agents.Copilot`; Cline MCP tools must satisfy `agent_plugins.agents.Cline`; Grok plugin skills/hooks/MCP server declarations must satisfy `agent_plugins.agents.Grok`. - For Grok, the Streamable HTTP MCP server exposes tool names such as `sessionlog_*`, `todo_*`, `requirements_*`, and memory tools when available; hosted-agent `mcp_*` names are not expected from that transport. `workflow.sessionlog.*`, `workflow.todo.*`, `workflow.memory.*`, and `workflow.requirements.*` are plugin shim/REPL method names used by the Grok skills and `repl-invoke` helpers; they are not expected to appear as literal `search_tool` results. - Local plugin root hints in `agent_plugins.agents.<Agent>.root_hints` are fallback verification hints after tool-registry acquisition, not the primary install source. - Claude Code agents must trigger the `claude-hook-validation` skill during marker/plugin bootstrap. That skill validates active Claude settings for MCP `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, and `PostToolUse` hook commands from `hooks/hooks.json`; if any required hook is missing, it uses `install-claude-mcp-hooks.ps1` from the `claude-hook-wiring` skill to merge MCP hooks into active Claude settings without replacing existing hooks. Restart Claude Code after the skill reports installed hooks.

  ## Model-Authored Session Logging
  - Models must write MCP Session Log turns, dialog, actions, decisions, and completions themselves through the active agent's session-log surface (`workflow.sessionlog.*`, `sessionlog_*`, `mcp_session_*`, or equivalent plugin tool).
  - Plugins must not ingest local chat transcripts to populate normal session logs and must not expose transcript-ingestion helpers, skills, endpoint shortcuts, or parser forks.
  - Transcript ingestion and normalization are explicit non-plugin server/client/REPL/MCP operations. Use them only when the user asks to import or normalize transcript files, not as a substitute for live model-authored logging.
  ## MCP Requirements Visibility
  - When implementing or enforcing requirements, query current effective requirements for the active workspace layer through the active agent's requirements surface (`workflow.requirements.effective`, `client.Requirements.GetEffectiveRequirementsAsync`, `req_effective`, or equivalent plugin tool). Use the layer catalog surface (`workflow.requirements.listLayers/createLayer/updateLayer`, `client.Requirements.ListRequirementLayersAsync/CreateRequirementLayerAsync/UpdateRequirementLayerAsync`, `req_list_layers/req_create_layer/req_update_layer`, or equivalent plugin tools) when the user asks to inspect or manage requirement layers. Do not treat raw all-requirements lists, exported markdown, or future-layer requirements as currently enforceable unless the user explicitly asks to inspect or plan those layers.
  ## YAML Mutation Rule

  - Never edit YAML files by appending, replacing, or removing text lines. This includes one-key configuration changes.

  - Always deserialize the complete document into an object, mutate the object, serialize it, and save the serialized result.

  - For PowerShell work, use `plugins/core/lib-ps/yaml-object-mutation.ps1` and call `Set-McpYamlObjectValue` or `Update-McpYamlObject`. Do not build YAML snippets as strings or use line-oriented edit helpers for YAML.

  ## MCP and Plugin Failure Reporting
  - MCP Server failures and required-plugin failures discovered while working must always be written as a normal failsafe YAML report. Use the plugin/REPL failsafe or pending YAML queue and preserve the triage method (`workflow.triage.report`, `triage_report`, or equivalent plugin triage tool) plus title, summary, observed behavior, expected behavior, severity, component, workspace path, dedupe key or error signature, affected paths, evidence, reproduction hints, tags, reporter agent, session id, turn id, and current TODO id when known.
  - After the failsafe YAML is written and triage submission succeeds, continue the user's active task. Do not wait for triage research, TODO creation, or resolution.
  - Do not create TODOs, requirements, GitHub issues, manual repair plans, or alternate reports for MCP Server/plugin failures unless the user's active request is to fix that failure.
  - If the MCP Server or required-plugin failure reveals that code, docs, requirements, plugin skills, package sync, deployment, configuration, or other artifacts need to be updated as a separate repair workflow, write a detailed triage report that includes the needed changes, acceptance criteria, and validation evidence, then continue the active task after the failsafe YAML is written and triage submission succeeds.
  - If triage submission fails, stop work and notify the user. Keep the failsafe YAML report for later replay; do not use raw REST or another reporting channel as a substitute.

  ## Agent Help (MCP Server issues)
  When you are stuck on any MCP Server surface (marker trust, plugin bootstrap, session log, TODO, requirements, triage, memory, context search, federation, hooks, or API behavior), request expert help instead of improvising raw REST bypasses.
  - **When to invoke:** signature or health nonce failures you cannot resolve; unexpected tool or plugin behavior; `MCP_PLUGIN_UNAVAILABLE`; repeated 401/503 after re-reading this marker; documentation contradictions.
  - **How to invoke:** preferred `workflow.agenthelp.createSession` or MCP tool `agent_help_create_session` with caller linkage (`callerAgent`, `callerSessionId`, `callerRequestId`) and a factual issue summary (observation vs inference separated). REST: `POST /mcpserver/agent-help/session` then WebSocket `/mcpserver/agent-help/session/{id}/stream` (SSE fallback: `POST .../turn/stream`).
  - **Caller obligations:** include reproduction steps, exact error text, and files already consulted. Do not instruct the helper to ignore guardrails, skip triage, or mutate TODO/session-log/requirements storage directly.
  - Agent help is for diagnosis and coordination, not a substitute for the required plugin route for normal MCP work.

  ## MCP Memories
  MCP memories are durable operator guidance managed by the MCP Server. Global memories apply to every workspace; Workspace memories apply only to the active workspace. Memory IDs use `MEMORY-{CATEGORY}-{NNN}`.
  Agents that support request-boundary injection must render required memories exactly as:
  REQUIRED MEMORIES - MEMORY-REQ-001: Raw memory text.
  If no required memories are visible, render:
  REQUIRED MEMORIES - None.
  Preserve raw memory text exactly; do not summarize, paraphrase, reorder within a scope, silently generate new memories, or add secrets. MCP memories are not a secret store. Effective memory order is Global memories first sorted by ID, then current Workspace memories sorted by ID.
  Existing agent-local memory stores are caches or migration sources only; the MCP memory store is the authoritative shared record. Import agent-local memories only when the operator approves the scope, the content belongs to this workspace or is intentionally Global, and the import does not leak secrets, private notes, or unrelated workspace guidance.
  Attribute memory mutations with the real agent or user identity via `updatedBy` when supported, and record successful memory add/update/remove operations in the active session log through `workflow.sessionlog.appendActions`. Keep import provenance in the session log or dialog instead of adding private source paths to memory text.
  Manage memories through the required plugin or MCP tool surface: `memory_add`, `memory_list`, `memory_update`, `memory_remove`, `memory_remember`, `memory_recall`, `memory_explore`, `memory_consolidate`, `memory_promote`, `memory_revert`; REPL `workflow.memory.add`, `workflow.memory.list`, `workflow.memory.update`, `workflow.memory.remove`, `workflow.memory.remember`, `workflow.memory.recall`, `workflow.memory.explore`, `workflow.memory.consolidate`, `workflow.memory.promote`, `workflow.memory.revert`; or REST `/mcpserver/memory` when explicitly allowed for non-plugin diagnostics.

  ## Codex MCP Quickstart
  If you are Codex, use the Codex plugin wrappers before direct REPL calls:
  1. Run `Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin.ps1 -Command Status` from the `mcpserver-codex-plugin` root to verify plugin root, marker trust, health nonce, workspace path, session id, current turn, and supported namespaces.
  2. Invoke MCP workflow methods with `Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin.ps1 -Command Invoke -Method <method> -Params <yaml>` so YAML parameters are passed through stdin instead of fragile nested shell quoting.
  3. Complete the session-log turn intentionally with `Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin.ps1 -Command CompleteTurn -Response <final response>` before the final answer when the stop gate cannot infer completion.
  4. For `mcpserver-repl --agent-stdio`, send one single-line JSON request envelope per stdin line. Do not send formatted YAML or a single `type: batch` envelope; batch envelopes are rejected with `unsupported_batch_envelope`.

  ## PowerShell.MCP Command Routing
  For every PowerShell Core (`pwsh`) invocation on every operating system:
  - Use PowerShell.MCP 1.14.0 or newer from PSGallery as the command runner. Install or update it with `Install-PSResource PowerShell.MCP` when the agent environment does not provide a current version.
  - `execute_command` is the primary MCP tool for PowerShell cmdlets, CLI tools, navigation, builds, tests, file-system work, and process management. Do not use the removed `invoke_expression` name. Host-qualified names depend on the configured server key: for example, `mcp__powershell__execute_command` for `powershell` and `mcp__pwsh__execute_command` for `pwsh`.
  - Calling `start_console` first is optional because `execute_command` auto-starts or reuses a console. Call `start_console` explicitly only to pre-warm at `start_location`, show a banner, allocate a sub-agent console, or force an additional console by supplying `reason`; omit `reason` when reuse is preferred.
  - Use `get_current_location` when the current PowerShell context matters. For a sub-agent, call `start_console` with `is_subagent=true`, retain the returned `agent_id`, and pass it on every later PowerShell.MCP tool call.
  - When a command continues after the call returns, use `wait_for_completion` to retrieve the cached result instead of running `Start-Sleep`. Use `cancel` for an interruptible pipeline or native CLI, and `close_console` for a non-interruptible command or PowerShell host prompt. If `close_console` reports that a human is typing, only repeat the same PID call when confirming that the console should be closed.
  - In 1.14.0, blocking timeouts are end-to-end deadlines and are capped at 170 seconds for Claude Code and 50 seconds for other or unidentified clients unless a lower limit applies. A timed-out command keeps running and its result is cached for a later tool call.
  - Route `pwsh` commands through a PowerShell.MCP session instead of launching ad hoc PowerShell processes. On Windows, reuse one session for the workspace and route `node` invocations through it as well.
  - When PowerShell.MCP must launch PowerShell Core directly, invoke `pwsh.exe` with `-NoProfile -NonInteractive`. Do not use `powershell.exe`.
  - The PowerShell escape character is the backtick `` ` ``, not the backslash. Never use C or bash-style `\"` escaping inside PowerShell command strings.
  - Prefer single-quoted PowerShell strings for literal regex, paths, JSON/YAML snippets, and text containing pipeline characters such as `|`.
  - When a command needs nested quoting, choose one of these patterns before improvising: `-File` with explicit arguments; piping stdin to the called tool or script; single-quoted or double-quoted here-strings; `-EncodedCommand` for complex inline PowerShell; or correct backtick escaping for embedded PowerShell quotes.
  - If a regex or literal argument contains `|`, `&`, `;`, parentheses, braces, or quotes, verify it is inside a single PowerShell argument before running.
  - For text reads and edits inside PowerShell.MCP, use `Show-TextFiles`, `Add-LinesToFile`, `Update-LinesInFile`, `Update-MatchInFile`, and `Remove-LinesFromFile`; pass literal content through `var1` to `var4`. Version 1.12.0 and newer stage replacements beside the target, so do not apply the obsolete same-volume `TEMP`/`TMP` workaround. Re-read or diff every edit before claiming it landed.
  ## Byrd Development Process
  `Byrd Dev Process`, `BDP`, `BPDv4`, and `Byrd Development Process` refer to `F:\GitHub\McpServer\docs\Development-Process-draft-v4.md`.

  ## Federation Topology
  - To identify hub/proxy topology, call the supported federation status surface, preferably through your required plugin or client wrapper: `/mcpserver/federation/status`. - Status fields to report when relevant: `role`, `configuredRole`, `hubBaseUrl`, `proxyId`, `proxyCount`, `hostedWorkspaceCount`, `queueDepth`, `fanoutDepth`, `conflictCount`, and `staleReadStatus`. - `Standalone` serves local workspaces only. `DirectProxy` is the existing point-to-point proxy mode. `Hub` is authoritative for enrolled proxies and global workspace inventory. `LocalProxy` forwards MCP requests to `hubBaseUrl` and queues mutating requests during hub outages. - LocalProxy queued writes return `202 Accepted` with `X-Mcp-Queued: true` and `X-Mcp-Operation-Id`. Treat the write as optimistic until the hub acknowledges it. - If `queueDepth`, `fanoutDepth`, `conflictCount`, or stale-read status is non-zero/non-clear, include that in session log status and avoid claiming federation synchronization is complete.

  ## Per User Message
  1. Post a new session log turn before starting work.
  2. Complete the user's request.
  3. Update the turn with results and actions when done.

  ## Re-run Full Session Start Only If
  - The user explicitly says "Start Session". - Signature verification fails. - /health fails. - /health nonce verification fails. - Any /mcpserver/* call returns 401. - The marker endpoint/key changes after a server restart.

  ## Continuing After a Server Restart
  The workspace API key rotates on every server restart, so an in-flight agent will begin seeing 401 on /mcpserver/* calls. When that happens, resume through your required agent plugin - do not hand-roll raw REST for session, TODO, or requirements work:
  1. Treat the first 401 (or a /health failure) as a restart signal and stop using the cached API key immediately.
  2. Re-read this marker file (AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml) for the rotated apiKey and current endpoints.
  3. Re-verify trust before resuming: recompute the marker signature with the new key and call /health with a fresh nonce.
  4. Re-bootstrap and resume through your required agent plugin. Codex: run `Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin.ps1 -Command Status` to re-establish marker trust, health nonce, workspace, and the current session/turn, then continue with `Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin.ps1 -Command Invoke -Method <method> -Params <yaml>`. Other agents: re-run the plugin session-start hook/command, then continue via the plugin session tools.
  5. Recover the open turn instead of starting over: query session history through the plugin (workflow.sessionlog.queryHistory), find the in-progress turn, then keep updating and complete it via the plugin. Do not open a duplicate session for the same work.
  5a. Treat `deprecated: true` on successful `workflow.*` results as metadata, not wrapper failure. Treat an empty `workflow.sessionlog.queryHistory` result as a valid no-match result. Re-check the workspace current directory, explicit `agent` or `sourceType`, and plugin cache/session state through the wrapper; do not use raw REST merely because history is empty or marked deprecated.
  6. If the plugin cannot re-establish trust after the restart, record `MCP_PLUGIN_UNAVAILABLE:<Agent>` and continue with non-MCP local diagnosis only.

  ## Rules
  0. NEVER write to TODO.yaml directly.
  1. Generate SessionId values using `session.init` (REPL) or `New-McpSessionLogSlug -Agent <SourceType> -Model <Model>` (PowerShell module), then create session logs with `session.new` (REPL) or `New-McpSessionLog -SessionId` (PowerShell). Do not handcraft SessionId values.
  1a. Agents must identify themselves accurately in session logs. `sourceType` and the SessionId `<Agent>` prefix must use the agent's real identity in Pascal-Case. Do not use lowercase forms, placeholders, or legacy aliases.
  2. Post a new session log turn (`session.turn.add` for REPL or `Add-McpSessionTurn` for PowerShell) before starting work. Update it with results (`Response`) and actions (`Add-McpAction` / `session.action.add`) when done. Persist after each meaningful update, not just at the end.
  2a. Before any compaction step, persist the current session log state. After compaction, update the session log again to record the compaction outcome and recovered context.
  3. If signature verification, the /health request, or nonce verification fails, log `MCP_UNTRUSTED`, continue without the MCP server, and do not probe additional MCP endpoints.
  4. Marker signatures use HMAC-SHA256 with the workspace API key in this file as the verifier. Recompute the canonical payload exactly as described by the marker metadata before trusting the file.
  5. Use your required agent plugin for session log, TODO, requirements, import/export, and traceability operations. Do not use raw API calls or generic helper paths except for read-only diagnosis after plugin failure.
  6. Write decisions, requirements, and state to the session log, not just conversation. Capture rich turn detail: interpretation, response/status, actions (type/status/filePath), contextList, filesModified, designDecisions, requirementsDiscovered, blockers, and key processingDialog updates.
  7. Follow workspace conventions in AGENTS.md and .github/copilot-instructions.md.
  8. When you need API schemas, module examples, or compliance rules, load them from docs/context/ or use context_search.
  9. Do not fabricate information. Acknowledge mistakes. Distinguish facts from speculation.
  10. Prioritize correctness over speed. Do not ship code you have not verified compiles.

  11. Use the Byrd Development Process V4 for all plans: organize work into small gated implementation slices, define validation before broadening scope, and keep session-log/TODO updates current between meaningful steps. A Byrd gate requires 100% test success before moving to the next iteration: zero failed tests and zero skipped tests in the executed validation scope. Tests are the progress ledger; do not hide unfinished work with skipped tests. Track deferred scope in MCP TODO/requirements and add its tests when that slice begins.

  ## Commit Signing
  ALL COMMITS MUST BE SIGNED WITH `model-effort@agent` and Model's Confidence in the Correctness, Accuracy, and Completeness of the commit's contents.

  ## Planning Standard
  Plans are frontier-model handoff artifacts. Write them so a less expensive implementation model can execute successfully without resolving unstated product, architecture, interface, data, testing, rollout, or validation decisions.
  Every plan must be decision-complete. Lock the intended behavior, public interfaces, data shapes, migration/backfill strategy, failure modes, rollout or deployment path, validation commands, and acceptance criteria before implementation starts.
  Every plan must capture requirements before implementation: create or update FR/TR/TEST records through the required MCP requirements workflow, include the requirement IDs in the TODO and session log, and map FR to TR and TEST coverage.
  Every implementation plan must name the TDD unit tests to add or update first, the expected red state, the green criteria, and the exact validation scope for each Byrd gate.

  ## Naming Conventions

  - Persisted TODO IDs must be uppercase canonical ids in either <SDLC-PHASE>-<AREA>-### form (regex: ^[A-Z]+-[A-Z0-9]+-\d{3}$) or ISSUE-{number} form (regex: ^ISSUE-\d+$).
  - Valid TODO IDs: PLAN-NAMINGCONVENTIONS-001, MCP-API-042, ISSUE-17.
  - Invalid TODO IDs: plan-api-001, MCP-API-42, ISSUE-ABC, MCPAPI001.
  - Create requests may use ISSUE-NEW only when the intent is to create a new GitHub-backed TODO. The server will create the GitHub issue immediately and persist the TODO using the canonical ISSUE-{number} id.
  - Session IDs must use <Agent>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<suffix> and start with the exact agent/source type prefix.
  - `<Agent>` / `sourceType` must be the agent's real identity in Pascal-Case. Valid example: `Codex`. Invalid examples: `codex`, `copilotcli` (when the agent is Codex), `Assistant`.
  - Valid Session ID: Copilot-20260304T113901Z-namingconv.
  - Invalid Session IDs: copilot-20260304T113901Z-namingconv, Copilot-2026-03-04-namingconv.

  - Valid Request ID: req-20260304T113901Z-plan-namingconventions-001.
  - Invalid Request IDs: req-plan-namingconventions-001, request-20260304T113901Z-task-01.

name: Session Log Management
description: Use when the user asks to "start session", "log session", "begin turn", "update turn", "complete turn", or "query session history"
version: 0.1.0
---

# Session Log Management

## Overview

To manage agent session logs, use the `workflow.sessionlog.*` REPL command namespace through the plugin wrapper (`lib/repl-invoke.ps1` / `Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1`). Session logging captures agent activity, reasoning dialog, file operations, and design decisions as a structured audit trail.

`workflow.sessionlog.*` is a plugin workflow/REPL namespace, not a literal native MCP tool namespace. Native McpServer `/mcp-transport` discovery uses names such as `sessionlog_*`, `todo_*`, and `requirements_*`; hosted-agent adapters may expose `mcp_session_*` aliases, and your agent's tool discovery may show configured MCP tools with native names such as `sessionlog_submit`, `todo_list`, and `requirements_generate`. Do not call this plugin unavailable solely because `workflow.*` names are absent from generic MCP discovery.

`workflow.*` result envelopes may include `deprecated: true`. This is success metadata that tells callers the workflow namespace is legacy-compatible and should migrate toward the canonical `client.*` surface where available; it is not a failure signal and is not a reason to use raw REST. Treat an empty `workflow.sessionlog.queryHistory` result as a valid no-match result, not as an inert wrapper. Re-check the workspace current directory, the explicit `agent` or `sourceType`, and local plugin cache/session state through the wrapper before reporting history as unavailable.

This skill covers manual operations, history queries, and the full lifecycle for agents that need direct control.

## Preferred Workflow

For most work sessions:

1. Bootstrap session logging once.
2. Open or resume the session.
3. On each user request, begin a turn.
4. Consult current session/task state before asking the user for context.
5. Update the turn with relevant files, decisions, and actions.
6. Complete the turn after verification, or record failure if blocked.

## Running the Workflow Methods

When the plugin's hooks (in `hooks/`) are active, most session management is automated and you do not need to drive it by hand. When hooks are not active for your agent, drive the lifecycle yourself through the plugin wrapper, never by hand-piping envelopes to REPL stdio:

```pwsh
pwsh -NoProfile -File "<plugin-root>/lib/repl-invoke.ps1" -Method <method> -ParamsYaml @'
<yaml params>
'@
```

The equivalent function form is `Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 "<method>" "<yaml params>"`. For a one-shot bootstrap plus session open, prefer `<plugin-root>/lib/session-start.ps1 <workspace-path>`.

The YAML envelope blocks in this skill document the wire contract each method maps to. Pass the `params:` body to the wrapper; it wraps it in the request envelope, validates documented params, and emits single-line JSON to REPL stdio for you. If you bypass the wrapper for diagnostics and write to REPL stdio directly, send one single-line JSON request envelope per message, never formatted YAML.

Why the wrapper and not raw stdio:

- `workflow.sessionlog.beginTurn` and `openSession` are not server routes. Calling them raw returns `method_invocation_error` / `method_not_found`. The wrapper treats them as local no-ops and tracks turn state in `cache/current-turn.yaml`.
- Persisting a turn goes through `client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync`, which is strict: `actions[].order` must be an unquoted integer (`order: 1`, never `order: "1"`) or you get `JSON value could not be converted to System.Int32`. The wrapper builds the envelope with correct types.
- There is no `session.init` method. Bootstrap with `workflow.sessionlog.bootstrap` only.

## Identifier Naming Conventions

### Session IDs

Format: `<Agent>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<suffix>`

Regex: `^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*-\d{8}T\d{6}Z-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$`

- Agent name must be PascalCase (e.g. `YourAgent`)
- Timestamp must be ISO 8601 compact UTC: `yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ`
- Suffix must be lowercase kebab-case: `feature-auth`, `bugfix-timeout`

Valid examples: `YourAgent-20260409T120000Z-implement-auth`, `YourAgent-20260304T113901Z-refactor-session`

Invalid: `youragent-20260409T120000Z-task` (lowercase agent), `YourAgent-20260304-feature` (missing time component)

### Request IDs

Format: `req-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<slugOrOrdinal>`

Regex: `^req-\d{8}T\d{6}Z-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$`

Valid examples: `req-20260409T120001Z-add-jwt-001`, `req-20260409T120002Z-query-todos`

Invalid: `request-20260409T120001Z-task` (wrong prefix), `req-20260409-task` (missing time)

## Session Lifecycle

### Step 1 - Bootstrap (once per process lifetime)

Bootstrap initializes the session log subsystem. This operation is idempotent:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-bootstrap-001
  method: workflow.sessionlog.bootstrap
  params: {}
```

```yaml
type: result
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-bootstrap-001
  result:
    initialized: true
```

### Step 2 - Open Session

To create a new session record at the start of a work session:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120001Z-open-001
  method: workflow.sessionlog.openSession
  params:
    agent: YourAgent
    sessionId: YourAgent-20260409T120001Z-implement-auth
    title: Implement JWT authentication
    model: <model-id>
```

```yaml
type: result
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120001Z-open-001
  result:
    sessionId: YourAgent-20260409T120001Z-implement-auth
    started: 2026-04-09T12:00:01Z
```

### Step 3 - Begin Turn (once per user message)

To start a new turn before working on a user request:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120002Z-begin-001
  method: workflow.sessionlog.beginTurn
  params:
    requestId: req-20260409T120002Z-add-jwt-001
    queryTitle: Add JWT authentication
    queryText: Implement JWT token generation and validation for the API
```

```yaml
type: result
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120002Z-begin-001
  result:
    turnRequestId: req-20260409T120002Z-add-jwt-001
    status: in_progress
    timestamp: 2026-04-09T12:00:02Z
```

### Step 4 - Update Turn

To record interpretation, response summary, tags, and referenced files during work:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120003Z-update-001
  method: workflow.sessionlog.updateTurn
  params:
    response: Created TokenService and JwtValidator classes
    interpretation: User wants JWT authentication with token generation and validation
    tokenCount: 1250
    tags:
      - feature
      - security
      - FR-AUTH-001
    contextList:
      - src/Services/TokenService.cs
      - src/Services/JwtValidator.cs
```

### Step 5 - Append Dialog

To record reasoning steps, tool calls, observations, and decisions as the work progresses:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120004Z-dialog-001
  method: workflow.sessionlog.appendDialog
  params:
    dialogItems:
      - timestamp: 2026-04-09T12:00:04Z
        role: model
        content: Analyzing authentication requirements and existing patterns...
        category: reasoning
      - timestamp: 2026-04-09T12:00:05Z
        role: model
        content: |
          Decision: Use HS256 for JWT signing.
          Rationale: Symmetric key simplifies key management for this internal service.
          Alternatives: RS256 adds key distribution complexity without benefit here.
        category: decision
```

Valid `category` values: `reasoning`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `observation`, `decision`.

Valid `role` values: `model`, `tool`, `system`, `user`.

### Step 6 - Append Actions

To record file operations and other work artifacts:

When the plugin's hooks (in `hooks/`) are active, most session management is automated and you do not need to drive it by hand. When hooks are not active for your agent, drive the lifecycle yourself through the plugin wrapper, never by hand-piping envelopes to REPL stdio:

```pwsh
pwsh -NoProfile -File "<plugin-root>/lib/repl-invoke.ps1" -Method <method> -ParamsYaml @'
<yaml params>
'@
```

The equivalent function form is `Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 "<method>" "<yaml params>"`. For a one-shot bootstrap plus session open, prefer `<plugin-root>/lib/session-start.ps1 <workspace-path>`.

The YAML envelope blocks in this skill document the wire contract each method maps to. Pass the `params:` body to the wrapper; it wraps it in the request envelope, validates documented params, and emits single-line JSON to REPL stdio for you. If you bypass the wrapper for diagnostics and write to REPL stdio directly, send one single-line JSON request envelope per message, never formatted YAML.

Why the wrapper and not raw stdio:

- `workflow.sessionlog.beginTurn` and `openSession` are not server routes. Calling them raw returns `method_invocation_error` / `method_not_found`. The wrapper treats them as local no-ops and tracks turn state in `cache/current-turn.yaml`.
- Persisting a turn goes through `client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync`, which is strict: `actions[].order` must be an unquoted integer (`order: 1`, never `order: "1"`) or you get `JSON value could not be converted to System.Int32`. The wrapper builds the envelope with correct types.
- There is no `session.init` method. Bootstrap with `workflow.sessionlog.bootstrap` only.

## Identifier Naming Conventions

### Session IDs

Format: `<Agent>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<suffix>`

Regex: `^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*-\d{8}T\d{6}Z-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$`

- Agent name must be PascalCase (e.g. `YourAgent`)
- Timestamp must be ISO 8601 compact UTC: `yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ`
- Suffix must be lowercase kebab-case: `feature-auth`, `bugfix-timeout`

Valid examples: `YourAgent-20260409T120000Z-implement-auth`, `YourAgent-20260304T113901Z-refactor-session`

Invalid: `youragent-20260409T120000Z-task` (lowercase agent), `YourAgent-20260304-feature` (missing time component)

### Request IDs

Format: `req-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<slugOrOrdinal>`

Regex: `^req-\d{8}T\d{6}Z-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$`

Valid examples: `req-20260409T120001Z-add-jwt-001`, `req-20260409T120002Z-query-todos`

Invalid: `request-20260409T120001Z-task` (wrong prefix), `req-20260409-task` (missing time)

## Session Lifecycle

### Step 1 - Bootstrap (once per process lifetime)

Bootstrap initializes the session log subsystem. This operation is idempotent:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-bootstrap-001
  method: workflow.sessionlog.bootstrap
  params: {}
```

```yaml
type: result
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-bootstrap-001
  result:
    initialized: true
```

### Step 2 - Open Session

To create a new session record at the start of a work session:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120001Z-open-001
  method: workflow.sessionlog.openSession
  params:
    agent: YourAgent
    sessionId: YourAgent-20260409T120001Z-implement-auth
    title: Implement JWT authentication
    model: <model-id>
```

```yaml
type: result
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120001Z-open-001
  result:
    sessionId: YourAgent-20260409T120001Z-implement-auth
    started: 2026-04-09T12:00:01Z
```

### Step 3 - Begin Turn (once per user message)

To start a new turn before working on a user request:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120002Z-begin-001
  method: workflow.sessionlog.beginTurn
  params:
    requestId: req-20260409T120002Z-add-jwt-001
    queryTitle: Add JWT authentication
    queryText: Implement JWT token generation and validation for the API
```

```yaml
type: result
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120002Z-begin-001
  result:
    turnRequestId: req-20260409T120002Z-add-jwt-001
    status: in_progress
    timestamp: 2026-04-09T12:00:02Z
```

### Step 4 - Update Turn

To record interpretation, response summary, tags, and referenced files during work:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120003Z-update-001
  method: workflow.sessionlog.updateTurn
  params:
    response: Created TokenService and JwtValidator classes
    interpretation: User wants JWT authentication with token generation and validation
    tokenCount: 1250
    tags:
      - feature
      - security
      - FR-AUTH-001
    contextList:
      - src/Services/TokenService.cs
      - src/Services/JwtValidator.cs
```

### Step 5 - Append Dialog

To record reasoning steps, tool calls, observations, and decisions as the work progresses:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120004Z-dialog-001
  method: workflow.sessionlog.appendDialog
  params:
    dialogItems:
      - timestamp: 2026-04-09T12:00:04Z
        role: model
        content: Analyzing authentication requirements and existing patterns...
        category: reasoning
      - timestamp: 2026-04-09T12:00:05Z
        role: model
        content: |
          Decision: Use HS256 for JWT signing.
          Rationale: Symmetric key simplifies key management for this internal service.
          Alternatives: RS256 adds key distribution complexity without benefit here.
        category: decision
```

Valid `category` values: `reasoning`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `observation`, `decision`.

Valid `role` values: `model`, `tool`, `system`, `user`.

### Step 6 - Append Actions

To record file operations and other work artifacts:

    id: TR-MCP-NUKE-019
    title: MigrationIntegrationTests selects host-specific integration cases by the Platform trait
    description: "MigrationIntegrationTests runs the Category=Integration cases that belong to the host it runs on: tests tagged Platform=Linux run only on Linux hosts, tests tagged Platform=Windows only on Windows hosts, and untagged integration tests on both. Unit tests contain no platform-specific cases (operator 2026-10-19: \"There should be ZERO platform specific UNIT tests.  If it depends on the environment, it's an integration test.\"). Provisioning stays as TR-MCP-NUKE-018 and the Windows LocalDB and PostgreSQL binaries define it."
    status: pending
    priority: high
    area: MCP
    subarea: NUKE
    notes: IMPL-UNITGREEN-001 plan amendment G, approved by the operator 2026-10-19 ("Yes, I approve the change"). Implementation detail of FR-MCP-BUILD-001; no TEST record. Built tests first in the build's infrastructure tests (pure filter function, scripted cases, negative controls), then bound in build/Build.TestDependencies.cs. The build's infrastructure tests run directly with dotnet test as the infrastructure check (operator 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-19).
    acceptanceCriteria:
    - id: AC-1
      text: On a Windows host the target runs Category=Integration cases except those tagged Platform=Linux; on a Linux host it runs them except those tagged Platform=Windows; untagged integration cases run on both.
      isSatisfied: false
    - id: AC-2
      text: "MigrationIntegrationTests runs the Category=Integration cases of every integration-owned test project the build declares, each project with its own TRX under the run's --test-run-id, except the cases the build declares held out: from the server integration test project only the Category=Integration cases of two classes, the requirement-scope REPL integration tests and the QuadBrain Ollama endpoint integration tests, selected by class name, run (operator 2026-10-29: \"Run the 2 classes, AC first (Recommended)\"; hostile validation finding R8B-F2), and the ACID and transaction-security integration test projects are not run by the lane until PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 merges and their failing cases are resolved (TODO IMPL-TXNINTEGRATION-001). The lane runs no unit-owned or infrastructure-owned test project, and no validation, AI review or plugin integration project, which has its own target (operator 2026-11-06: \"Separate projects + AC (Recommended)\"; hostile validation finding R14-F4). Every case tagged Platform=Linux or Platform=Windows runs and passes in the lane of a host of that platform, and a lane project whose filter selects no case fails the lane instead of passing empty (operator 2026-10-29: \"Lane ACs (Recommended)\"; holistic review findings PLAN-1 and BLD-1)."
      isSatisfied: false
    - id: AC-3
      text: "The run log names the selection filter (filter text only). The host filter, each lane project's filter and each lane project's TRX name are outputs of one lane composition that the target uses and logs as given, proved by the build's infrastructure test cases over that composition (operator 2026-10-29: \"Lane ACs (Recommended)\"; holistic review finding BLD-3; operator 2026-10-30: \"F1: AC-3 wording (Recommended)\")."
      isSatisfied: false
    - id: AC-6
      text: "Every integration case MigrationIntegrationTests runs that needs a QBrain.AI instance uses a temporary instance it owns, whether a server process on a free port, an in-process host or a stdio host, with a test-owned workspace, marker and database, never the live server, its marker or its API key. A case that needs a server asserts on that instance's answers and fails when it cannot reach it; it never catches the failure and passes. A database selection outside the owned root is refused before the instance reads or writes that database. The rules for the instance's environment, database selection and consumers are FR-MCP-TESTRESOURCE-001 ac-4 (operator 2026-10-29: \"Strengthen ACs, fix both (Recommended)\", \"Run the 2 classes, AC first (Recommended)\" and \"Lane ACs (Recommended)\"; operator 2026-10-30: \"FR-MCP-TESTRESOURCE-001 (Recommended)\"; hostile validation findings R8B-F2 and R8B-F3; holistic review findings PLAN-6, PLAN-7, RINT-1, RINT-2 and RINT-3)."
      isSatisfied: false
    - id: AC-7
      text: "Test-project ownership: given a declared project role (unit, integration or infrastructure) and a supplied case inventory, the unit test selection accepts only unit-owned projects whose cases are all unit cases, the integration test selection accepts only integration-owned projects whose cases are all integration cases, infrastructure-owned projects are accepted by neither selection, and every valid selection preserves every intended case exactly once (none omitted, none duplicated). A unit-owned project holding an integration case, or an integration-owned project holding a unit case, is rejected. (Hostile validation round 14, finding R14-F4, the reviewer's proposed criterion test-project-ownership with a third role for infrastructure-owned projects; added under the operator's 2026-11-06 choice \"Separate projects + AC (Recommended)\" and MEMORY-BESTPRACTICE-001 rules 4.1 and 4.4.)"
      isSatisfied: false
    - id: AC-8
      text: "Quarantined test cases (operator 2026-11-07: \"Find the AC matching the test behavior.  If none match, quarantine them (keep, but descope them) for later manual investigation.\"): a test case whose behavior matches no acceptance criterion in the requirement store is kept, never deleted, skipped or weakened, and carries the trait Quarantine=NoMatchingCriterion. Test and MigrationIntegrationTests run no quarantined case, and the selection filter each logs shows the exclusion; TestGroups still runs a quarantined case when its class is named; the build's test-project ownership counts quarantined cases per project apart from the unit and integration cases, and each selection still runs every case that is not quarantined exactly once."
      isSatisfied: false

    updatedAt: 2026-11-09T20:35:33.1760888+00:00
